| **`FolderLoadCoordinatorTests.LoadAsync_SecondFolderWhileFirstScanBlocked_FirstLoadIsDroppedSilently`** | Failed real GitHub Actions CI 3x in one day (2026-09-27, #197/#198/#193). **Reproduced locally** (2-core CPU affinity + repeated full `App.Tests` project runs, ~30-50% hit rate over ~15 runs; a single isolated run of just this test never reproduces it). Added a temporary low-overhead trace (`ConcurrentQueue`, no I/O during the race -- `Console`-based tracing suppresses the race entirely, a classic Heisenbug) and captured one failing run's log. **Key clue:** the trace shows the SLOW load's own guard check (`loadToken.IsCancellationRequested \|\| !_clock.IsFolderCurrent(loadGeneration)`) reading `cancelled=False, currentGen=1` (i.e. *matching its own, not-yet-superseded generation*) and PASSING -- meaning at that point in real wall-clock time (by queue-insertion order in the trace, not just timestamps), the FAST load's `_clock.NextFolder()`/`_loadCts.Cancel()` prologue call had **not yet run**, even though the test's source code calls `await coordinator.LoadAsync(@"C:\fast")` (whose synchronous prologue should run inline, before any yield) *before* `releaseScan.Set()` (which is what let the slow load's blocked scan resume and reach that guard check at all). This is either a genuine async-ordering violation somewhere between the test and `FolderLoadCoordinator.LoadAsync`'s synchronous prologue (not yet located), or a subtlety in how `Task.Run(Func<T>, CancellationToken)` interacts with a token cancelled *while the delegate is already blocked inside it* that differs from the assumed "delegate observes cancellation via `ThrowIfCancellationRequested` and that's authoritative" model. All temporary instrumentation was reverted (not committed) -- repro recipe and the trace excerpt above are the starting point for whoever picks this up. | Needs a dedicated, focused session (not squeezed into an unrelated PR): reproduce with the same 2-core-affinity recipe, re-instrument, and specifically verify whether `coordinator.LoadAsync(@"C:\fast")`'s synchronous prologue genuinely runs before its first `await` returns control to the test in this exact call chain (it should, by C# semantics, but the evidence says otherwise) -- check `_explorerOrder.TryGetSnapshotProgressiveAsync`'s fake implementation for any synchronous blocking/yielding before the coordinator's own generation bump, and check whether `ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace`/`ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf` or anything else ahead of `_clock.NextFolder()` could defer it. |
